claim: verdict_mentions tracks neither fences nor code spans, so hypothesis verdicts quoted from the role template's own skeleton close the hypotheses and check goes green with the questions unanswered
scenario: references/hunter.md:85-87 sits inside the ```markdown "Report structure" fence (opened at line 69) and already carries the substituted block id: `T1.1 — checked: <what exactly proves it>`, `T1.2 — not checked: …`, `T1.3 — not applicable: …`. Reproduced end to end on a scratch project: a hunter report that quotes that skeleton inside a fence and answers nothing gives `hypotheses H1` → "closed 3/3" with verdicts checked / not checked / not applicable, and `check` exits 0 printing "review state is consistent". Three questions were never asked and no gate is red. LIMITS_PLACEHOLDER exists because an agent copied this same template into the coverage-limits section.
invariant: 1 (check must not go green on a false state); 4 (a word inside a code span or a fenced block is not a verdict)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: A table whose first row is data rather than a header is taken for a table of hypothesis verdicts: every numbered row carrying a vocabulary word becomes a verdict on the hypothesis of that number
scenario: table_about_hypotheses is decided from the table's first row only. Run on the parser: a headed gate table (`| # | gate | test | mutation |` then rows) yields {} — the 2151 fix holds — while the same table written without a header row, `| 1 | state vs definition | none | confirmed |` / `| 2 | status vocabulary | test_x | not checked |`, yields {'T1.1': 'checked', 'T1.2': 'not checked'}. The T1 acceptance criterion asks for exactly such a gate→test→mutation table. Either hypotheses are closed by rows that are not about them, or check reports "gives hypothesis T1.2 different verdicts" and demands that a correct report be rewritten.
invariant: 4 (report parsing tolerates live reports, but shape is not a verdict)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: A vocabulary word inside a code span decides the verdict: the lookaround around n/a guards \w and / but not backticks, brackets, quotes or parentheses, and the earliest word in the line wins
scenario: Measured with verdict_word_at: `n/a` → 1, "n/a" → 1, (n/a) → 1, [n/a] → 1; only a/n/a and curation/n/a.ts are refused. Of a 25-line matrix run through line_verdict, four diverge: "T1.7 — the `n/a` token in a path is handled; checked by test" → not applicable; "T1.8 — `checked` is only a code span here, in fact not examined" → checked; "T1.15 — the report says `not checked` but I did check it" → not checked; and "T1.9 — the block moves to verified after the report" → checked on the bare word "verified". hypotheses, check and summary all carry the wrong answer and no gate goes red.
invariant: 4 (a word inside a code span is not a verdict)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: A ~~~ fence is not recognised by section_body, section_items_full or demote: a column-0 # line inside one truncates the manifest's Hypotheses section and the hypotheses below it vanish
scenario: Run on the parser: a manifest listing hypotheses 1-4 with a ~~~markdown block between 2 and 3 whose first line is `# heading` gives hypotheses("T1", …) = ['T1.1', 'T1.2'] — two of four. The same manifest with a ``` fence gives all four, and a 4-space indented code block is harmless. check then demands two verdicts, gets them and passes; hypotheses_sha fingerprints only the truncated text, so later edits to 3 and 4 are not tracked either. demote() has the same blind spot: it pushes the heading inside the ~~~ fence down a level when the manifest is pasted into the prompt.
invariant: 1 (check must not go green on a false state); 6 (a fingerprint covers the whole reviewed text)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: file_sha and block_lines read the working tree, not the index: for a file present in the index but not on disk the fingerprint degrades to the file's name and its lines drop out of the readability count
scenario: Reproduced in a scratch repository: with src/api.ts laid out, block_sha = 4cfb25c46484160a and block_lines = (3 files, 5 lines); after `rm src/api.ts` with the index untouched, ls-files still lists it, file_lines still returns 3 from the index, but file_sha returns None, block_sha becomes 14f3f778131f964d and block_lines becomes (3, 2). From then on the file contributes only its name: its contents can be rewritten and check never reports "block files changed after the review", and a block far above the readability ceiling passes the "cannot be read in one session" gate. file_lines' own docstring names sparse checkout as the real case.
invariant: 5 (git is the source of file truth, not the disk); 6 (a fingerprint covers the whole reviewed text)
root: file truth read from the disk instead of the index

claim: The fix-commit gate compares a raw path with `git show --name-only` output, which quotes non-ASCII paths, so a finding on a Cyrillic-named file can never be marked fixed
scenario: Reproduced end to end. In a scratch repository `ls-files -z` prints src/модуль.ts while `git show --name-only` prints "src/\320\274\320\276\320\264\321\203\320\273\321\214.ts" (core.quotePath defaults to on). A commit touching both src/модуль.ts and "src/plain file.ts" was marked as the fix for two findings: `set-finding … fixed --commit <sha>` succeeded for both, and `check` then reports for ever "commit <sha> does not touch src/модуль.ts" while the path with a space passes. In a lang:ru project the gate is red on a truthful state and the only way out is a --fixed-in naming a file the fix did not touch.
invariant: 5 (paths are handled NUL-separated); 1 (check must be trustworthy in both directions)
root: git output parsed as plain text, without -z / quotePath

claim: Twenty-four checks in cmd_check have no test: each was silenced in a copy of the kit and the suite stayed green, while silencing a covered gate turns it red
scenario: Measured by mutation, one gate per mutant. Silencing any of these leaves `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` green: state/definition both ways, manifest missing, verifier report missing, declared and hunter reports absent, running without a timestamp, unparsable timestamp, running over 24 h, duplicate finding id, empty field, nonexistent block, severity/confidence/status vocabulary, external fix-commit form, fixed without a commit, duplicate without dup_of, rejected-but-open, claim and scenario caps, findings.md divergence, unowned files, missing hypotheses fingerprint, proof vocabulary. Three controls go red, so the harness does detect a silenced gate.
invariant: 2 (every check comes with a test, and the test is proven by a mutation)
root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: guard-grep.sh silently skips a scan path that does not exist and exits 0, so a gate goes green when a package is renamed — the opposite of what its own header promises
scenario: Reproduced: `guard-grep.sh --pattern '\.Publish\(' --marker 'outbox-allowed:' -- internal/billing` reports the violation and exits 1 while the package is there; after `mv internal/billing internal/payments` the same command prints nothing on stdout and nothing on stderr and exits 0. A typo in the path behaves identically. `[ -e "$path" ] || continue` drops the path and `[ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ] || exit 0` exits clean, so CI is green, every forbidden call in the moved package is unguarded, and the failure is indistinguishable from success.
invariant: 1 (a gate that cannot go red on a wrong state); 3 (a refusal names the way out)
root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: import assigns ids by position to rows without one: a finding inserted above the numbered rows takes an id that already exists, and both records keep it with no way back through the tool
scenario: Reproduced: `import H1` numbers two findings H1-001, H1-002 and writes the ids back into the block file. A new row without an id prepended to that file and re-imported becomes H1-001 as well — the register then holds two H1-001 ("NEW prepended" and "first"). `check` reports "finding H1-001: duplicate id" and names no way out; `set-finding H1-001 rejected --reason r` reaches only the first match and leaves the second open. The only repair is editing findings.jsonl or the block file by hand, which the kit's own rule forbids.
invariant: 11 (import is idempotent for the same draft); 3 (a refusal names the command that fixes it)
root: hand-assigned ids without a uniqueness check

claim: A block definition written by hand is never validated: a missing slug, phase, role or goal gives a KeyError traceback instead of a refusal naming the fix
scenario: Reproduced by adding {"id":"H2","title":"Payments","paths":["src/x.py"]} to blocks.json the way setup invites (it writes "blocks": [] for a human to fill in). `status` → KeyError: 'phase', exit 1; `order` → KeyError: 'phase', exit 1; `summary` → KeyError: 'slug', exit 1; `prompt H2 --role hunter` → KeyError: 'slug'. With phase supplied and slug missing, `check` — the gate that exists to catch a broken state — dies the same way at manifest_path as soon as the block leaves todo. Exit 1 reads as "the state is red", not as "your definition is malformed".
invariant: 12 (a traceback reaching the user is a defect; exit codes mean something); 3 (a refusal names the command that fixes it)
root: hand-edited input reaches the code unvalidated

claim: stale_tree returns None without refs/remotes/origin/HEAD and says nothing, so the freshness gate is silently inert for a checkout with no remote or with a remote not named origin
scenario: Reproduced on git 2.55: a repository with no remote, and one whose only remote is named `upstream` (symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD → "fatal: not a symbolic ref"), both give `check` exit 0 with no mention of freshness however far behind the tree is. That is the vendored copy of a neighbouring service the threshold comment was written for — twelve days stale, the hole closed, the verifier "confirming by execution". The hunter's CI example is wrong on current git: `git remote add origin` + `fetch` does create origin/HEAD, so the residue is no-remote and non-origin checkouts.
invariant: 2 (a gate whose mechanism is inert is not a gate)
root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: run-role.sh writes the spend line to the journal whatever the run's exit code, so a run cut off by --max-turns is recorded as an ordinary completed run
scenario: Reproduced with a stub `claude` that writes a partial stream and exits 1: run-role.sh prints "claude exit: 1", then appends "hunter — spend: 0 min, None turns, … cost estimate $0.00" through `$REVIEW log` and exits 1. RC is captured at line 35 and not consulted until the final exit; neither the line nor axes.py looks at result.subtype or is_error. The journal is the only memory the next session has, and it now says the block was hunted, with no word that the assignment was truncated. (A failing `review prompt` does exit 2 before the journal, leaving only a zero-byte prompt file in TMPDIR.)
invariant: state lives on disk, not in the conversation; the turn cap is the safety switch and its trips must be visible
root: spend recorded without its outcome

claim: commit_file_sets parses `git log --name-only`, which prints only the new path of a rename and quotes non-ASCII paths: coupling and order undercount churn and drop files silently
scenario: Measured on this repository: review.py has 41 first-parent commits with --follow and 9 under its current path (R090 review.py → skills/review-kit/…, R099 → skills/finetooth/…), and `git show --name-only` on the rename commit prints only the new path. `order` therefore ranks T1 — the block covering the file the kit turns on — on 22% of its real change frequency, and that ranking is the whole product of the command. In a project with Cyrillic file names those paths never match `owned` (which comes from ls-files -z) and are invisible to coupling altogether, so a seam between two blocks cannot be reported at all.
invariant: 5 (git is the source of file truth; paths are handled NUL-separated)
root: git output parsed as plain text, without -z / quotePath

claim: The named-files gate is a plain substring test, so a longer path that contains an owned path satisfies the gate for both: a report naming src/api.ts.snap marks src/api.ts as named
scenario: Run on the gate's expression with owned = ['src/api.ts', 'src/api.ts.snap', 'src/x.py'] and the report text "I read src/api.ts.snap and src/x.py": missing = []. Any file whose path is a prefix of a sibling's — a snapshot, a .map, a .test.ts next to a .ts, an index.ts under a longer directory — is closed by naming the sibling. The gate was built to stop the "read 25 of 25" claim, and this is the cheapest way past it that does not even require intent.
invariant: 1 (the gate must not be satisfiable without the state it asserts)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: On a history of 20 commits or fewer mass_cutoff equals the largest commit, so no mass commit is ever skipped and the initial whole-tree commit pairs every file with every other
scenario: Run over synthetic histories of sizes 1..100: for n ≤ 20 the cutoff equals the largest commit (12 → 12, 19 → 19, 20 → 20) and the guard is a strict `>`, so nothing is skipped; from 21 on it starts to bite (21 → 20, 100 → 96). On a young repository `coupling` therefore treats the initial commit containing the whole tree as an ordinary change, and three formatting sweeps reach together ≥ 3: the output is a wall of pairs that say nothing about a seam, while order's churn counts every block as touched by every sweep. The threshold comment promises exactly the opposite protection, and a new repository is when coupling is run.
invariant: 8 (a number must hold where it is applied)
root: threshold that does not hold at the edge of its range

claim: summary --aged slices its machine block with text.index(' -->') and json.loads: a block title or path containing ' -->' gives a traceback instead of the drift table
scenario: Reproduced: a block titled "Import --> export pipeline" is written verbatim into the machine block, and `summary --aged sum.md` then cuts the JSON at the first ' -->' inside the title — json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string, exit 1. A title ending in '-->' fails the same way. The user gets a traceback from the one file that is meant to outlive docs/review/, and the file's own heading says "do not edit", so there is no sanctioned repair.
invariant: 12 (a traceback reachable from a legal command line)
root: hand-edited input reaches the code unvalidated

claim: Without a result event axes.py reports turns None, cost $0.00 and an output count its own comment calls a stream artefact, in the format of a real measurement; a truncated last line raises
scenario: Reproduced on synthetic streams. Complete: "spend: 10 min, 42 turns, … output 21k, cost estimate $3.41". The same stream with the result event removed — what a killed or capped run leaves: "spend: 0 min, None turns, … output 0k, cost estimate $0.00", exit 0, and run-role.sh writes that to the journal, recording an expensive truncated run as free. The same stream with its last line cut short: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, exit 1 — under `set -e` in run-role.sh that costs the journal line, the agent's reply and the run's exit code.
invariant: the spend measurement is what the turn caps are derived from
root: spend recorded without its outcome

claim: init rewrites updated_at on every run, so a no-op re-run always dirties state.json
scenario: Reproduced: two consecutive `init` runs on an unchanged definition differ only in updated_at (2026-09-24T14:50:59Z → …T14:51:00Z); every other key is identical. CI that runs `review.py init && review.py coverage --no-write && review.py check` and then asserts a clean working tree — the usual shape for a generated-artifact gate — fails on a correct state, and the honest workaround is to stop running init in CI, which is what the gate existed to guarantee.
invariant: 11 (init, coverage, findings, backfill, restamp re-run without changing a correct state)
root: none (single instance)

claim: The verifier's coverage-verdict gate matches the bare word 'complete' anywhere in the report, so 'I completed the check' satisfies a gate meant to demand a statement about what was left unreviewed
scenario: Reproduced end to end: a verifier report whose whole body is "I completed the check of every finding; nothing was confirmed." passes verify_report_problem (returns None) and `check` exits 0 on the block. COVERAGE_VERDICT matches "complete" inside "completed", so a verb about verdicts answers the question about coverage — the very distinction the neighbouring hunter gate is strict about. The Russian half fails the other way: "Проверка завершена полностью" and "все находки проверены" match nothing, so an honest ru report is rejected.
invariant: 1 (the gate must not be satisfiable without the content it demands)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: Four thresholds carry no measurement or reference: REF_LIST_LIMIT=80, the 200-character 'manifest nearly empty' bound, CLAIM_MAX=220 / SCENARIO_MAX=700 and COUPLING_HUB_BLOCKS=6
scenario: Read against every other constant in the file, each of which carries its source (READABLE_LINES 6000 from measured runs and the MSR 2022 study, STALE_TREE_DAYS 7 from the twelve-day incident, ROOT_RULE_AT 3 from variant analysis, COUPLING_MIN_TOGETHER/MIN_SHARE from the first project and Zimmermann et al.). A project whose manifests are terse fails "manifest is empty or nearly empty" at 199 characters and nothing in the file says whether 200 is defensible; the same question about 80 reference files or 6 hub blocks cannot be answered by reading. Tuning them becomes taste, and the next constant added follows the precedent of the bare ones.
invariant: 8 (every number has a source next to it; a bare magic number is a finding)
root: threshold without its source

claim: prompt substitutes into the pasted manifest text and blames the role template for a leftover placeholder that in fact came from the manifest
scenario: Reproduced: a manifest paragraph reading "The template uses {{HUNTER_NOTE}} and {{FILES}} as placeholders" makes `prompt H1 --role hunter` exit 2 with "template hunter.md has substitutions left without a value: {{HUNTER_NOTE}}" — hunter.md contains no such placeholder and the author edits the wrong file. The quieter mirror also reproduces: with only {{FILES}} left, the manifest's own prose renders as "The template uses src/api.ts\nsrc/api.ts.snap\nsrc/x.py as placeholders", because FILES is substituted after MANIFEST.
invariant: 3 (the message must lead to the fix)
root: hand-edited input reaches the code unvalidated

claim: One marker exempts every hit in the window below it, not just the call it was written above — the exact failure guard-grep.sh was written to replace grep -B with
scenario: Reproduced: a file with `// outbox-allowed:` on line 2 and broker.Publish( on lines 3, 4, 5 and 6 (default window 3) reports only line 6 — one escape hatch silently exempted three calls. The header states the opposite as the script's whole reason to exist: "grep runs consecutive hits together into ONE block … a marker granted to the first call silently exempts the second one three lines below it" and "here each hit is paired with the marker by LINE NUMBER … so a marker covers exactly the call it was written above and nothing else". The rewrite reproduces the defect it names, so a gate adopted on that promise lets through every forbidden call within three lines of an existing hatch.
invariant: 1 (a gate that cannot go red on a wrong state); 3 (the documented behaviour must be the real one)
root: a gate that cannot go red

claim: listed() runs git ls-files with check=True, so a pathspec in blocks.json that git rejects makes check and coverage die with a CalledProcessError traceback instead of naming the bad pattern
scenario: Reproduced: a paths entry of ":(nosuchmagic)src" — a typo in the pathspec magic the kit invites projects to use for exclusions — makes `check` exit 1 with subprocess.CalledProcessError on `git ls-files --stage -z -- :(nosuchmagic)src`, and `coverage` exit 1 the same way, while `status` exits 0 because it never expands the pattern. git's own message ("Invalid pathspec magic") is swallowed, so the user sees a Python stack trace and an exit code that reads as "the state is red". The neighbouring gate at 2458 handles a pattern that matches nothing; a pattern git refuses to parse has no handler.
invariant: 12 (a traceback reachable from a legal command line); 3 (a refusal names the command that fixes it)
root: hand-edited input reaches the code unvalidated

claim: The cited-line gate is guarded by isinstance(line, int), so a finding whose line is written as a string skips the check entirely while findings.md still renders it as a real location
scenario: Reproduced: two identical open findings on a 3-line file, one with "line": 9999 and one with "line": "9999". check reports only the first ("line 9999 is cited, but src/api.ts has 3") and says nothing about the second, yet findings.md renders both as `src/api.ts:9999`. The gate is described in its own comment as "the cheapest sign of fabrication"; a draft findings file is hand-written JSONL, where a quoted number is an ordinary slip, and import copies the field through untouched.
invariant: 1 (the gate must not be silently skippable); 12 (a field outside its type is a refusal, not a pass)
root: report parser matches shape, not meaning

claim: [R1-001, fix review round 1] The new guard for "a gate that cannot go red" does not see a gate whose message is not a literal
scenario: run against a copy of the kit. Adding to `cmd_check` ```python if st.get("review_id") != defn.get("review_id"): msg = f"review_id mismatch" problems.append(msg) ``` — a gate with no test at all — leaves `GateRegistryTest` green (rc 0) and the whole suite green (205 tests, OK). The same holds for `problems.append(dup_problem(...))`. Written with a literal message instead, the identical gate turns `GateRegistryTest` red. So the guard covers one of the two shapes the tool actually uses, and the shape it misses is the one three existing gates are written in — the next gate added by copying its neighbour is untested and nothing says so.

claim: [R1-002, fix review round 1] `summary --aged` now counts one file under two names — the opposite of what the change claims
scenario: reproduced end to end. A repository whose base commit is followed by two commits — one touching `src/a.ts` and `src/b.ts`, one touching `src/b.ts` — gives `summary --aged`: ``` HEAD: H1 commits: 2 files: 3 <- two files exist dev: H1 commits: 2 files: 2 <- correct ``` The same run against `dev`'s `review.py` prints 2. Every file that is first in one commit and not first in another is counted twice, so the drift table over-reports on any real history, in the one file that is meant to outlive `docs/review/`.

claim: [R1-003, fix review round 1] The named-files gate now refuses a report that writes `./src/api.ts`
scenario: reproduced end to end. A block owning `src/api.ts` and `src/util.ts`, with a hunter report whose coverage list is ``` - ./src/api.ts - ./src/util.ts ``` gives `check` exit 1: "H1: 2 of 2 block files are not named by full path in any report (src/api.ts, src/util.ts)". The same report passes on `dev`. The report is honest and complete; the gate refuses it, and the author's only repair is to rewrite the paths.

claim: [R1-004, fix review round 1] A quoted verdict still closes a hypothesis when it is quoted by indentation or by `>`
scenario: run on the parser, block id `T1`: | report body | verdicts read | |---|---| | ` ```markdown ` … `- T1.1 — checked: <what proves it>` … ` ``` ` | `{}` — fixed | | a four-space indented block holding the same line | `{'T1.1': ['checked']}` | | `> - T1.1 — checked: <what proves it>` | `{'T1.1': ['checked']}` | | `<!-- - T1.1 — checked: … -->` | `{'T1.1': ['checked']}` | A report that restates its assignment as an indented example, or quotes the template with `>`, closes its hypotheses without answering them and `check` prints "review state is consistent" — the same false pass T1-001 describes, through a neighbouring door.

claim: [R1-005, fix review round 1] `axes.py` changed which `result` event it measures, and this is in no report and under no test
scenario: a stream carrying a 40-turn `success` result and a 2-turn `error_max_turns` result reports, in either order, `spend: 10 min, 40 turns … $5.00` with no outcome word — the cut-off marker in the shorter event is dropped. The heuristic is defensible (a capped run has the most turns by construction), which is exactly why it needs to be written down: nobody re-derives it from the diff. In the same round the kit's own journal gained `spend: 0 min, 2 turns, 329 tool calls … cost estimate $67.92` — a line that reads as a measurement and cannot be one — and neither `axes.py` nor the guards added beside it say so.

claim: [R1-006, fix review round 1] The changelog's Breaking section holds five fixes that are not breaking, and not the change that is
scenario: a user upgrading a running review reads the Breaking section to find what they must act on and is told that "`SKILL.md` description said three roles" is a breaking change, while the change that really does break a running review is not there: `blocks()` now validates every block definition, so a `blocks.json` that worked yesterday can refuse every command today. Measured, dev vs HEAD, same repository: ``` phase written as "1" dev: status rc=0 HEAD: status rc=2 "has no whole-number `phase`" goal written as "" dev: status rc=0 HEAD: status rc=2 "has no `goal`" ``` Exit 2 on `status`, `order`, `summary`, `prompt` and `check` alike. The refusal itself is the fix and is right; its absen …

claim: [R1-007, fix review round 1] Two new rules in the fix role template, recorded nowhere
scenario: a later editor reworks `references/fix.md` — the file is T2's subject and T2 has not run yet — and drops either rule. Nothing goes red, nothing in the changelog says the rules were ever there, and the next fix phase bumps the version again and re-runs the suite in ten worktrees, which is the cost these two rules were written to stop (329 turns, most of it ceremony, measured in this very round).

claim: [R2-001, fix review round 2] A verdict inside a fence nested in a list item still closes a hypothesis
scenario: reproduced end to end, `check` rc 0. A hunter report whose hypotheses section is ~~~ ## Гипотезы - Задание просило написать вердикт так: ```markdown - H1.1 — проверена: <чем доказано> - H1.2 — проверена: <чем доказано> ``` Ни на одну гипотезу я не ответил. ~~~ gives `hypotheses H1` → `H1.1 checked`, `H1.2 checked`, `closed 2/2`, and `check` prints

claim: [R2-002, fix review round 2] The gates that read a report's substance still count quoted text
scenario: reproduced end to end, `check` rc 0, twice. 1. A verifier report whose entire body is `Шаблон просит написать так:` followed by a ```` ```markdown ```` fence holding `- H1-001 — подтверждена: воспроизвёл.` and `Охват полный, непрочитанного нет.` — nothing verified, nothing stated — passes `verify_report_problem`, and the block stays `verified` with `check` printing "review state is consistent". This is the gate whose own docstring says "an empty `*.verify.md` alongside a full hunter report moved the block to `verified` without an independent check", and it is the same gate T1-019 (medium) was filed against. 2. A hunter report whose `## Ограничения охвата` section holds only a fence …

claim: [R2-003, fix review round 2] The new quotation guard cannot see a parser that does not exist yet
scenario: measured. A new function added to `review.py` ```python def report_sections(md: str) -> list[str]: out = [] lines = md.split("\n") for line, fenced in zip(lines, fenced_lines(lines)): if not fenced and line.startswith("#"): out.append(line) return out ``` leaves `SourceRuleTest` **green** (4 tests, OK) — a parser that reads a `>` quote, an indented example and an html comment as the report's own words, with nothing to say so. It is not hypothetical: `verify_report_problem` (R2-002) is that parser today, and the guard does not see it either.

claim: [R2-004, fix review round 2] `a/` and `b/` are accepted as prefixes, so a real `a/` directory closes the gate for a file nobody read
scenario: reproduced end to end. A block owning `src/api.ts` and `a/src/api.ts` (a repository with a top-level `a/` directory) whose report names only `a/src/api.ts`: `check` exits **0** and says nothing about `src/api.ts`, which no report mentions. On `7a7b944` the same report is correctly refused (`names_file("- a/src/api.ts", "src/api.ts")` → `False` before, `True` after).

claim: [R2-005, fix review round 2] `run-role.sh` dies on the truncated stream `axes.py` was taught to survive
scenario: measured on a stream whose last line is `{"type":"assis`. `axes.py --journal` prints `1 unreadable line(s) · spend: …`; the same file through the run-role snippet exits 1 with `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError`. Under `set -euo pipefail` that is the script's last command, so `exit $RC` never runs: an operator whose run was killed (`claude` exit 143) or cut off sees a Python traceback and the exit code 1, and anything scripted on top of `run-role.sh` reads the wrong ending.

claim: [R3-001, fix review round 3] the nested-fence fix silently truncates a manifest again, and `check` goes green on it
scenario: A manifest item quotes an example: an opening fence 4+ spaces past the list column (no blank line), a list line inside it, then the closing fence. The closing fence was read as an OPENING one and swallowed the rest: 4 hypotheses became 1, check rc 0. Reproduced on HEAD of round 3 (closed 1/1) vs 850ed21 (closed 1/4).
